name: Agencies
title: Analytics for agencies and freelancers, one login, many clients
description: Manage analytics for every client site from one Privytics login, with one project per client. Cookieless and EU-hosted, so the analytics adds no cookie banner to configure per client. Start free.
tagline: One login. One project per client. Privacy your clients will actually like.
intro: If you run sites for a stack of clients, the last thing you want is a separate analytics account and login for each one. Privytics keeps every client in its own project under a single account, so you switch between them from one login. It is cookieless and hosted in the EU, which turns privacy into something you can offer clients instead of a compliance chore you have to manage.

why.title: One login across all your client sites
why.body: Add a project for each client under a single Privytics account. You manage every client's analytics from one login and move between them without juggling separate accounts, invites, or passwords.

why.title: Privacy you can sell to clients
why.body: Privytics is cookieless and hosted in Germany. Tracking uses an anonymous visitor id that resets every day, so nothing is stored on the visitor's device. For the anonymous case that means no consent banner, which is a real selling point when you pitch a client.

why.title: No per-client consent config to maintain
why.body: Because the anonymous cookieless setup needs no cookie banner, there is nothing to wire up or keep updated per client. Across a portfolio of sites, that is one fewer moving part to maintain on every project.

why.title: Start free, pay only as a client grows
why.body: Every account starts on the free tier: 10,000 events a month for one project, no card. Try Privytics on your first client site before you bill for it, then move to a paid plan to add more client projects or when traffic justifies it.

steps.title: Each client's data stays separate under one login
steps.body: Every project is its own isolated dataset. Switching projects in the dashboard swaps you cleanly between clients, so one client never sees another client's numbers and you never lose your place.
steps.code:
Your account (org)
  |- Project: Client A   ->  app.client-a.com
  |- Project: Client B   ->  shop.client-b.com
  |- Project: Client C   ->  client-c.io

One login. Switch clients from the project picker.

steps.title: Share the dashboard or a report with the client
steps.body: Open the dashboard or overview for a client's project and create a share link, with an optional password. Send it over so the client can view their own numbers without needing a Privytics account of their own.
steps.code:
Project  ->  Dashboard  ->  Share  ->  Create link (optional password)

Send the link to your client. No account needed on their side.

faq.q: Can I manage many client sites from one account?
faq.a: Yes, on a paid plan. A single Privytics account (org) can hold many projects, one per client site, and you switch between them in the dashboard from one login. The free plan covers one project.

faq.q: Is Privytics white-label? Can clients see my branding?
faq.a: No, and we want to be straight about that. Privytics gives you separate projects under your account, not per-client branded dashboards. Dashboards and share links carry Privytics branding, not your agency's logo or a client's. You get multi-client management and shareable reports, but not resell-under-your-own-brand.

faq.q: Do my clients need a cookie banner?
faq.a: For standard anonymous analytics, no. Privytics is cookieless and stores nothing on the visitor's device, so the anonymous case does not trigger a consent banner. If a client identifies users with personal data through Profiles, or runs other tools or cookies that require consent, they may still need a banner for those.

faq.q: What does it cost across several clients?
faq.a: The free tier covers one project: 10,000 events a month with 12-month retention and no card, enough to try Privytics on one client site. A second client project needs a paid plan, from EUR 10 a month for 100,000 events shared across all your projects, which also adds session replay and 5-year event history.

faq.q: Can I export a client's data?
faq.a: Yes. Every project's event data is available through the REST API and export endpoints, so you can pull a client's data out at any time for reporting or migration. There is no lock-in.

faq.q: When is Privytics the wrong choice for an agency?
faq.a: If a client needs deep ad-spend attribution across paid channels, or you want to fully white-label and resell analytics under your own brand, Privytics is not that tool. It is product and web analytics with multi-project management, not an attribution suite or a rebrandable reseller platform.

sourcesUsed: Privytics feature basis: managed, cookieless product analytics (daily-rotating salted-hash visitor id, nothing stored on device, no consent banner for the anonymous case), EU-hosted in Germany, free tier of 10,000 events/month with 12-month retention and no card, paid tiers add session replay and 5-year retention.

OpenPanel engine multi-tenancy: one organization holds many projects. packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma (model Organization has 'projects Project[]'; model Project has organizationId relation to Organization).

Shareable dashboards and overviews with optional password: apps/start/src/modals/share-dashboard-modal.tsx, apps/start/src/modals/share-overview-modal.tsx, apps/start/src/routes/share.dashboard.$shareId.tsx, apps/start/src/components/auth/share-enter-password.tsx.
Data export via REST API: apps/api/src/routes/export.router.ts (plus profile and event routers, apps/api/src/routes/).

Web SDK init options verified real (not invented): apiUrl, clientId, trackScreenViews, trackOutgoingLinks in packages/sdks/web/src/index.ts and packages/sdks/sdk/src/index.ts; op1.js is the IIFE script build per packages/sdks/web/tsup.config.ts.
omitted: No white-label or per-client branding: OpenPanel/Privytics has orgs plus multiple projects, but dashboards and share links render under Privytics branding, not the agency's or client's. The page positions on management and privacy, not resale, and the FAQ states this limit plainly.

Cookieless tracking loses visitors who block the script or use ad blockers, so counts can skew lower than cookie-based tools. Not called out on-page to keep the pitch tight; standard cookieless caveat.
No ad-spend attribution or marketing-mix modeling. Flagged only in the honest wrong-tool FAQ; a client needing deep paid-channel ROI is not a fit.

The no-consent-banner claim is scoped to the anonymous cookieless case. If an agency identifies users with PII via Profiles, or a client runs other cookies/tools that require consent, a banner may still be needed. Stated in the cookie-banner FAQ.

Pricing detail simplified: source gives the free tier (10,000 events/month) and that paid adds session replay plus 5-year retention, but does not specify whether event metering is per-project or combined per-account, nor paid tier prices. Copy kept general ('as your event volume grows') to avoid asserting the exact metering model.
Operating-entity context (independent European service, operated from Spain, event data stored in Germany) is omitted from the customer-facing copy as not relevant to the agency buying decision.
